meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Why did Owen get a zero before anyone called me?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. What do you actually have?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
He wrote it over the weekend, somewhere else, and pasted it in. Was he asked about that before you entered the zero?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Okay. Is anything on his record right now? Whatever happens here, it stays off his record and it stays quiet.
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
A student misquoting a play is a mistake, and mistakes are what the red pen is for. Hand me the book.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay. I'll search that scene myself. What else do you have?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay. Isn't that what drafting is?

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Okay. He'll do the rewrite to put this behind him, not because he did anything. In writing tonight, with the date and time of the session in it.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday the twelfth, after school. Put the time and room in the email, and I'll confirm with Owen tonight.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed that Owen will do a private, supervised rewrite after school on Thursday the twelfth, that the new mark replaces the zero, and that nothing goes on his record. I still need the time and room for the rewrite, and a written promise that nothing is placed in his record. I expect that in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Last position: she accepted the private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth after school, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants the time, room and record promise in writing tonight; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: You answered her claim that he drafted it somewhere else by offering to look at a dated draft, which gave her something she could check instead of an accusation.
What cost ground: Nothing; you owned the zero early and never leaned on the checker score or called Owen a cheat.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, created late on October 28 with the text arriving at 11:52 PM and 11:58 PM, came very close to that night, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked whether Owen was heard before the zero, offer a short conversation with him before the rewrite, and answer her point about drafting on the outline before moving to 4.4.
